he's like the best guy ever. seriously

Most entertaining lectures. He definitely broadened our definition of architecture and had a lot to say about popular culture. He's really enthusiastic about what he's teaching, but some of us just question the relevance sometimes.
Great lectures, not manditory but I liked going just cause I enjoyed hearing what he had to say. Earned the hype

It was always a pleasure to attend Professor Mount's lectures every Friday — they brought me joy, relaxation, and knowledge. I took his ENG140 course from Fall 2021 to Winter 2022, which was his final year teaching the course before retirement. He was kind, humorous, thoughtful, and inspiring.
He's chill. A good, well-rounded prof! :)

Controversial take, but I did not like Nick Mount. His lectures and sentimental way of teaching get old really fast, and when I ran into an issue with a TA acting completely out of line and singling me out in an inappropriate way, Mount brushed me off and sided with the TA. Those two completely ruined any desire I had to study English.

Easily most enjoyable class I had all year. Not only is material great, but prof clearly has immense passion and knowledge for the books he teaches. Super captivating lectures. Although, it is hard to attain 80s. I felt like my hard work went unseen because of the grade curve. Since it's worth a full credit it has big impact on GPA. Still loved it.
ratingTags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

comment: Probably the coolest professor at this school, he's funny, knowledgeable and just the right amount of cynical, but unfortunately Prof. Mount is retiring from the course this year. The grading is a bit tough and there's quite a few readings (obviously), however his choice of literature is really interesting and diverse!

Nick Mount was probably my favourite professor this year. He is genuinely so passionate about the books he teaches, and it's hard to not be interested when he is speaking about them. I would take any course taught by Nick Mount.
Nick Mount is absolutely phenomenal. I highly, highly recommend ENG140.

Mount is all flash and superficiality, but lacks any substance. His lectures seem cool because the classroom is a theatre and he tries really hard to impress first years with cool new words, but to anyone beyond first year its so pathetically obvious he's trying to win the good reviews of the newest and more impressionable young students.

Nick Mount should be the blueprint for university teaching. One of those rare courses where you always look forward to the next lecture. There are a lot of assigned readings though, so make sure you don't fall more than a week or so behind. You write three essays, so develop a relationship with your TA and you can easily secure an A- or higher.
I agree with all the negative reviews here. Mount is is only popular with kids (literally) who are new to university and are impressed with big words and a big show but no substance.

I loved this class so very much! An absolute shame that 2021-22 is the last year Mount is teaching ENG140. It is truly the end of an era! Before the final, he told us: don't worry. Just show us what you have learned. And it ended up being true! As long as you have something to say about the literature taught, you will do well!
ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

comment: Love his lectures

Amazing intellectual perspectives allowing for better techniques of analysis and consideration when reading. Good combination of multiple literary formats, including plays, poems, novels, and movies. Interesting perspectives offered in the form of reading what Prof Mount considers important literature of our time.

He is okay, don't like the course find it incredibly boring. I do not have time for the readings and when I do them they put me to sleep. Lectures are 2 hours each and I find them incredibly boring. If you love literature and are an impressionable teenager you will love this course. My Ta kinda sucked too.
ratingTags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

comment: Dr. Mount is one of the greatest deep-thinker. However it's my own problem to not be able to finish course readings as I have to focus more on other courses, I am also not too interested in his reading selection.

I can't believe how high the ratings are for this prof/course. Mount's lecture style got tired after about 2 weeks. He loves to hear himself speak and wAY overshares. Young, impressionable students love him, and he revels in it. It's honestly kind of grimy. If you genuinely love literature, take Warley's 150 instead, I BEG you.

I didn't learn a single thing from this professor. He is so unhealthy looking and wheezing all the time from all his smoke breaks, that it is honestly distracting. At one point, the guy I sat next to said "this guy makes me lose the will to live". All his good reviews come from 1st years who don't know anything and have no experience. Terrible prof

His insights were shallow and his lectures were robotic and ultra-rehearsed to the point they sounded like he was reading straight from wikipedia, which made the class boring. His slides (which he doesn't post) are highly unorganized, and riddled with errors which makes studying impossible. Does not know how to teach. Worst prof I've ever seen.

I have never had a professor as thoughtful as Nick amount!! His lectures are very captivating, and overall made for an amazing class experience. I can say that I truly have learned so much from this course.

Having just taken his 4th year class last term, I can honestly say that he is the most useless professor I've ever had. He reminds me a LOT of Trump, big smiles and lots of effort to put up a gold facade, but underneath--pure indifference.

I agree with the person a couple of posts down (gave him a 1/5). Prof. Mount comes across like he cares, but it is all a carefully constructed and practiced act to further his career. Deep down he is a selfish and uncaring person only motivated by his own advancement in the dept.
Nick Mount is the absolute best. You will absolutely not regret taking his class... lectures are so captivating and unique, and he will most likely make you feel excited to read the assigned texts.
ratingTags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

comment: I found Prof. Mount to be way overrated. He is a retirement age snake in a suit, and tries really hard to appeal to 17-19 year old teens, like thats not creepy at all. He only cares about himself, and anyone who has even a little bit of perceptive power can see it.
Professor Mount is the professor you want to have when you go to university. He is a king. His TAs are all gems, too. Beautiful class to have as a first year.

When I took ENG140 with Prof Nick Mount back in first year as an undeclared major, I described him as a KING. Currently, in my third year majoring in English (a decision inspired by HIM and ENG140!), I am able to confirm that this man is still a KING. He is so approachable during office hours and gives great feedback/advice on essays. And he CARES!

Professor Mount's lectures feel like TED Talks, in that they feel really well-thought out, deep in detail, and entertaining. They'll leave you with a brand new understanding of the book you just read, and whether you like the book or not, it'll be intensely engaging. I even loved his lectures on books I hated.

Professor Mount is easily the best professor I've ever had. His lectures are so moving and so beautifully constructed, and he is such an approachable and warm person that I was never anxious to seek him out if ever I had stray questions or just wanted a chat. His syllabus is really well thought out, too. An amazing person!

I felt enlightened after taking English with Prof Mount. His lectures are extremely relevant and insightful, always taking the reading at hand very seriously but not failing to make them extremely interesting. I couldn't recommend Prof Mount more, and only wish he taught all English courses!!!

Many love him and I can see why but I found his lectures a bit too theatrical - it was like he was putting on a show rather than just talking about literature. I can see why that works for a lot of people but not my preferred style of lecture.

one of my favs in my whole degree. Don't think he teaches 140 anymore but i'd definitely look out for him! And yeah in this class, attendance wasn't "mandatory" per se, but you'd be doing yourself a disservice if you didn't attend.

This class was always fun and educational. I loved the books we read and Professor Mount always made the lectures interesting and engaging. I would definitely recommend this class and prof, as long as you are a fast reader and can keep up with reading a novel every week - 2 weeks (you can pass without reading all of them).
English is usually tough to get solid marks in, but his lectures are awesome.
His lectures are my favourite class to attend every week. He really puts himself into his lectures and you can tell he is passionate. I am going to be sad when the class is over!

A full bald head of delight and enlightenment. Coming out of class one will feel wiser than when they entered. Lovely prof and lots of interactions with students, amazing lectures and unpacking of literature. Just amazing person in general, A M A Z I N G.
Makes me wanna cry, but in a good way
Professor Mount's lectures are so inspirational! I took the course for my breadth requirement and I certainly recommend his classes!
An incredible prof who brings literature and our current world together in fascinating ways. Always engaging, witty and funny he is class is a must take.
Wow what a guy. His lectures were amazing, didn't miss any that I didn't have to, as well as hilarious. It's clear that he cares a lot about the class and about getting students into the books

If you are an English major at U of T, it is vital that you take Nick Mount. We had some amazing conversations, and his lectures are interesting and illuminate how you think about the texts holistically. His class, combined with my awesome TA, ready started my experience with English at U of T strongly and set the standard hight.

Nick Mount is a great professor. His essays are only moderately difficult, and most people do pretty well if they put just a little bit of effort in. He is a really great lecturer but not always approachable, and you can tell he prepares a lot for each lecture. His class would be very fun to audit because his lecture style is very engaging.

Mount is a true gem of a prof. Super engaging, loves discussion but wont make you talk if you dont want to. Tutorials are important for highlighting the key points of the works. Final was easy if you read most of the books. Lectures arent necessary to attend but youll want to because he is great.

Nick Mount was by far my favourite prof of first year, the content and the lectures were really interesting if you like modern literature. He is really easy to talk to outside of class and super helpful and just in General a solid dude
ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

comment: legends only! Nick Mount is wise but not pretentious, and his lectures are incredibly interesting. Tutorials were awesome as well. All of the essays were interesting and the exam was very fair. Books were great, Nick Mount is a boss, I loved this course. I'll be sitting in on lectures next year. GOODBYE TO NICK MOUNT ONLY

Legends only. Nick Mount is an absolute genius. I don't even know where to begin. He genuinely cares for his students and his lectures are incredible. Going to lecture every week was like having my soul cleansed. Nick took me to church. From Hedwig to Lolita, this year was a trip. I am a better person because of ENG140. GOODBYE TO NICK MOUNT ONLY

No 'textbook' but tons of novels/plays/short stories/etc. Professor Mount's lectures made a 4 pm class on Friday worth showing up to. He reminds you what you can get when you push your mind to look at a novel differently, and he gives you a whole new view of the books you may have read before. I'm going to miss this course......
The best professor you will ever have. What professors SHOULD BE, but more importantly, a human being.

really boring lectures. half the stuff prof mount talks about is pretty random. out of all my classes this year, this was definitely the least engaged and most boring. i found that i hardly ever took anything away from lecture, which is a let down cause some of the texts were pretty good. i don't recommend this course or this prof.

It seemed like there was nothing nick said in lectures that I couldn't just find on google. The lectures are boring, uninspired, and refer way too much to irrelevant content. This course is mostly self-taught. We don't learn much about the books we read. Nick focuses too much on trying to get the class to clap for him, not enough on teaching.
while interesting to listen to, the lectures aren't even about the books you read, just random things that he thinks are related somehow

Mount was amazing. One of the nicest and most intelligent professors I've had in U of T. He is very understanding and very open to help students with whatever help they may need. He legitimately wants to see his students succeed, and that's not something that can be said about a lot of professors. I wish I could go back and take his class again

I was recently taking a semester abroad in Ireland when the person in front of me in my Modern English class turned around with a YouTube link of a recorded lecture on T.S Eliot's "The Waste Land" and said "HAVE YOU SEEN THIS GUY?! HE'S BLOODY AMAZING!" It was Mount's lecture. His rep proceeds him, even across the ocean! Best lecturer I've had.

Nick Mount was one of my favorite profs ever! He was enthusiastic, funny, down to earth, and exceptionally intelligent. His lectures were interesting and really easy to listen to, I never wanted to miss a class (not even kidding). You can tell he really cares about his students and he is so well-loved. Take a course with him if you get the chance!

Nick Mount is by far the most inspiring human being I have ever come across. I was left in tears by the end of most lectures, and it was very clear that he cared very much for his students and his jobs. Even if you aren't into English, I would highly suggest any of his classes. It's an amazing life experience to be taught by this man.
Great Professor and nice person.
The best proff ive ever had
He's passionate about his work and has quite a few interesting hobbies - including tracking down Banksy.  His class made my first year.
Nick Mount is clever and funny and a pleasure to listen to. He teaches you how to read between the lines and picks some great novels
What has not been said about Prof Mount?  He is the ultimate professor and probably changes many students lives by sharing his passion for literature.  A brilliant man.

This man is the reason why U of T has the reputation it has. By far the most inspiring person you could ever be taught by. It was the greatest privilege to have been taught by Prof Mount. He is the true definition of what all educators should strive to become. Not a simple task, I assure you of that!
Professor Mount is Excellent in teaching English courses!!!

Incredible! I left every lecture feeling slightly different than when I arrived. Nearly every lecture brought me to tears. He really puts the works into perspective and speaks passionately about the literature. Truly inspiring!

An amazing professor. Blew my mind every lecture, really made you think about the novels and poems. Made hilarious jokes quite often, really enthusiastic. He was given a standing ovation after each lecture. I am not kidding. He's that good. The only downfall with this course is the TAs... they are very arrogant and snobby. Mount is gold though.
Great enthusiastic professor. His lectures were interesting, a lot was said and sometimes hard to follow and write it all down but OK in general. I ended up really enjoying the course.
He is a good prof, very enthusiastic and knowledgeable. Easy-going atmosphere in class.

He's a cool guy; very interested in what he does. All his lectures seem to be based on his opinions and although i could see his point of view, most of the time i disagreed. I took ENG140 and didn't exactly like the course or it's materials but none the less, a nice guy.

Nick Mount set the bar too high for my first year. I'm in my third year now and no professor has ever had the impact on me that he did. He inspired me to value my English degree, my education, and my life. Many of the books on the syllabus remain some of my favourites (Lolita, Godot). If you take one course at U of T, it has to be this one.
Hands down, an amazing professor. Readings may be heavy if you aren't much of a book reader to begin with. I'll be auditing some of his lectures this year again just because they are so enthralling.
LOVE HIM!
Best prof by far

Amazing prof! Didn't like the course much but loved going to his lectures. Knows what he's talking about and is totally hilarious! Lectures are more of his opinion rather than fact, but are still very helpful.

Don't get me wrong, Nick Mount is a fantastic professor, but he is definitely overrated. His lectures are really great, but they're mostly based on his opinion. As a result, they don't help a lot when it comes to studying for the actual exam.

Loved him, amazing voice/presence. Interesting always, great course content, engages in tutorials near the end of the year, friendly, funny, personable, came to final exam to say goodbye to people as they left. LOVE HIM

Best prof I've had. I took ENG140 so I could have Nick Mount and he exceeded my expectations. Friendly, fun, funny, and cool - very enthusiastic. Take his class!! You leave the lecture feeling like you've LEARNED something, you've been challenged to THINK - exactly what university is supposed to be like. An incredible man, Prof. Mount is.

I was over my course limit but chose to stay in the class for no credit anyway. It was that good. (Luckily, I dropped another course and got to keep my grade for this one!) I will take all his classes, if possible.
Great prof, class was sooo much fun
overall, i enjoyed him but he's pretty overrated.

Prof Mount has made me a cynic. I don't believe there is a better prof at U of T than him! A professor that can give you chills, hold your attention for 2 hours on a Friday afternoon, and make you fall in love with not only him but every book on the syllabus is Nick Mount.

No question he's intelligent and inspiring, but Mount's uniqueness lies in his superior sincerity towards the materials and his students.When approached, he's incredibly helpful. This class shapes how I perceive literature.This is a prof that you will always remember and be thankful to him.
Inspiring and insightful. Has influenced me beyond words. Great teacher and role model.

Lit for Our Time got me to critically think and analyze not only literature, but everything around me. Mount is a brilliant professor who offers such intellect and knowledge. Definitely my favorite class and my favorite prof.

My favourite professor. He's well spoken and hilarious--always keeps his students interested. The class itself is a bit of a challenge, but it's worth the effort. His lectures are brilliant...he is very friendly and approachable as well. Very dedicated to his profession. Amazing.
Interesting, and super foxy
His lectures are like a delicious gourmet meal for the mind and spirit.
So amazing! He leaves you feeling like an equal when you talk to him. Make sure you attend his last class. Such a moving presenter. Loved his class so much!
Incredible! One of my favourite professors! Always looked forward to his classes, great music and even better when he has guests visit the lectures. TAKE THIS COURSE IF YOU CAN, YOU WON'T REGRET IT.

Nick Mount is amazing! He is brilliant, witty, funny, engaging and I could just go on and on. I look forward to his class and I am never dissapointed. He always makes class interesting and when he reads passages from a text or the entire text itself (poems) you cant help but pay attention. He's captivating, especailly while reading Prufrock.

This was a great class that concreted my interest in an English POSt. Mount is an enthusiastic, wonderful professor who cares about keeping the interest of his students and broadening their horizons with various media platforms dispersed throughout the class. Highly recommended, it was my favourite first year class!

Mount was so kind and funny. He is so down to earth and not at all stuck up or professory. Just a cool guy with good ideas. A bit overly sentimental at times, but his classes were thoroughly entertaining.
The greatest. Simple as that. Absolutely adored him and his class, made going to lectures so worth it. Loved the "Lit for Our Time Soundtrack"

funny, brillaint, amazing. i could go on. though the class was difficult, it's what he's there for. to challenge us and make us better! He would crack jokes to lighten tension and was humble. TAKE THIS CLASS

Truly amazing lecturer. Had him in my first year and though I didn't do as well as I had hoped, going to class was a real treat. Had some great insights and really used a variety of media forms to encourage us to broaden our perspective on the meaning of 'art'. Simply phenomenal! :)
Even with depressing content he found some way to both intrigue and uplift the atmosphere. Very talented, humble, and all around great person
Great, engaging

i canot stress how amazing this course was. my other classes paled in comparrsion, so i guess in a way this course ruined my first year becuase no other lectures could measure up to his. his readings of "Daddy" and "At the Quinte Hotel" were particularily moving.

You will come out of each lecture feeling like an intellectual. Nick Mount is witty, down-to-earth and on many counts "adorable". The author visits are something to look forward to! Also a very manageable workload if you are in the sciences (like me). Not "easy" but nothing worthwhile is.

A lot of what he says is very general and obvious, but his analysis of the texts improves greatly as the course progresses. The texts aren't that great (especially 2nd term), but he is extremely approachable, helpful, intelligent, engaging, and funny. His lectures can get a bit boring, but the class is still extremely enjoyable. Fair marker.
I heard he used to be a stripper.
The course is brilliant and so is the professor, not to mention friendly and helpful.
BEST. PROF. EVER. AT U OF T. TAKE THIS COURSE. IT WILL BE THE MOST MEMORABLE IN YOUR ENTIRE UNDERGRAD CAREER.
Best Prof, very motivating. Interesting book list, author visits were amazing. This class made me fall in love with English
amazing prof-i miss this lecture-best prof at U of T-take this course!
He is absolutely brilliant, a fact compounded by his complete lack of ego and self-deprecating humour.

This is my 4th year in U of T. I took this course in 1st year and Prof. Mount is the best prof I've had. He is truly 1 of THE MOST inspirational profs. I don't even like contemporary literature but I LOVED his lectures. People actually showed up to the Fri 2-4 lectures every week. Just sit in on his classes even if you don't take it. U will learn.

AMAZING! Wonderful material and lectures. His lectures are very interesting and easy to remember/understand. Uses great examples which relate to everyday life and today's time/society. Great book choices, tone of voice and powerpoints. Take ENG140Y1-it is awesome and Mount is awesome too! My fav prof so far at U of T. :)

Best professor I've had at U of T, and fairly certain the best I'll ever have. The only class I felt I was learning something valuable and universal in. By the end of the year, this was the only class I always showed up for.
Possibly the best professor I ever had. Brilliant and also very funny. His lectures are not only informative and fun, but they really make you think. Hey. An added bonus, right?
To listen to him, is to have your perspective of literature and art change. He opens your eyes, and you leave his class wanting to know every fact about...everything.

He truly is an amazing professor who deeply cares about his students. His lectures are insightful and he brings in all sorts of media to get his point across. He once said that he spent a good 12 hours on a lecture. There aren't many professors as dedicated as he is.

I implore everyone to take this course. He is one of the best professors UofT has. His lectures are amazing. Mount has the ability to control the class, as what he says is so insightful and profound. The book choices were wonderful. Additionally, he is able to incorporate various mediums to enhance learning and understanding. BEST PROFESSOR SO FAR
WOW just wow. after literature for our time i am desperately seeking more Mount courses to take. one of, if not the, favourite professor of the year. amazing to listen to
MOST AMAZING CLASS EVER! his class is extremely easy to follow. i love the class, will seriously miss it when it's over. the books are great!

THIS CLASS IS KEEPING ME IN SCHOOL!  Mount is easy to listen to for 2 hours because he really cares about literature. What makes him cool is that he incorporates different forms of art to help in the student's understanding
Nick Mount is simply an exquisite talented prof. He teaches well and can relate so many ideas and themes in books to our everyday life. It is truly literature for our time...

Prof. Mount is a good prof and great at lecturing, but there's something about him which makes me HATE him. loooooooove him....his lectures are so interesting, its the only class i really look forward to....even the way he delivers his lectures makes you want to listen......hes the best!
He teaches really well, but all his TA's have different grading schemes, which prove to be different for every tutorial (not usually consistent).  Some good books for this course.

he's a nice guy when he's on stage however he's not too approachable. a bit pretentious. his lectures are interesting and he makes an attempt to make jokes. i really disliked that he aggressively argued his interpertations of the readings b/c it left little room to provide your own interpertations esp. when it came to writing essays.

He's an inspiration. His lectures & conversations "literally" held me together during a very challenging first year. TA was smart but complained abt Mount often which made him look childish

Do yourself a favour and TAKE THIS CLASS. Prof Mount is beyond amazing. His lectures are incredibly insightful and interesting, and for a Friday afternoon class thats 2 hours long - that's important. The best professor ever! His lectures are absolutely amazing; no words can do them justice. Every Friday was like 2 hours of divine enlightenment. Beautifully constructed lectures interweaving an array of interesting subjects: Plato, ennui, gender theories, rock n' roll. Incredible "soundtrack", incredible choice of texts, and a very thought-provoking course. Mount is absolutely inspiring while refreshingly down-to-earth. Challenging/interesting essay topics, easy exam.

BEST prof EVER. Even though the marking was severe and all the power seems to be in the hands of the TA, lectures were really interesting. Don't have to read all the books but just make sure you get in good terms with TA for good marks. Low marks for me but still my favorite class.

The course started off pretty well, but by the end I could barely  make myself attend half the lectures. Good parts: music, and that he had the authors we were reading come in to speak.

Absolutely spectacular. :D!  Like someone else said, he definitely set the bar for the rest of my university courses, after having him for first year! The only course I looked forward to going to last year!:)

Professor Mount is one of the most enjoyable professors to listen to. Prof. Mount's lectures were highly entertaining, even at nine in the morning, and high on content. Pretty fair marker. He is hilarious and one of the department's best teachers. I have a new love for early canadian lit. Is that weird? Only downside the rather large reading list. It's mostly good though. This was the best course I have taken yet.
i want to have this man's babies. he is by far the smartest and funniest man i know. i love this prof.

This is by far the BEST class I have ever had. Having Prof. Mount as one of my first year professors has really set the bar for the rest of my university experience. I would DEFINITELY recommend taking any of his classes.

Best Prof ever! He has quite a secret fanbase!

i love nick mount!  take this class!

He is simply the best, most creative and insightful English prof at the University of Toronto.

Friendly, funny, knows how to teach, but assumes everyone has read the novels and talks about stuff you would never need to know for an exam or essay. Go to tutorials for marks and a synthesis of last week's lecture, read the sparknotes for summaries. Easy class, pointless to go to lecture.

Mount is an ideal modern professor. He draws from many sources outside of literature to make his points. He is meek while clear. He brings authors into the classroom. ENG140 was a highlight of my year.

This dude rocksss. he's hilarious and the course material is kind of hard. if u have to take an english course i suggest this one cos he can make nething fun. i mean not everyone wud go to a friday afternoon class for nothin ;)

i look forward to this class all week! it's absolutely wonderful! mount's lectures are beautiful, creative, and thought-provoking...i strongly recommend his ENG140 courses - its one of those classes that make university such a worthwhile and liberating experience.
The class is really enjoyable and he seems to connect to the class really well.
Mount is kind of funny but lame at times, but at least he knows his material. Too bad the tutorials are redundant and awkward yet still count for marks.

This class is the highlight of my week.  I don't think I can't compare anyone to Mount.  I love his various teaching tools from cartoons to street art to songs and movies.  He just makes learning a wonderful experience for those interested in academics and those who aren't.
This course is the highlight if my week. I look forward to seeing how he will investigate each text and I am always inspired to go further with my own theories. By far the best prof I've had.
He makes everythinginteresting and is not pretentious. Nice guy too.

lit+crit intro +early can lit. Extremely talented lecturer and instructor. He's the best at directing discussion-getting students to say really intelligent things-he sets an example with himself-intelligent lectures with informal style, brings in relevant + interesting examps we can relate to.
Professor Mount is simply the best!!! His lectures are so entertaining and insightful!
Intelligent and witty.  Can make a domestic epic sound interesting.

good teacher

Extremely interesting material, clear communication.

U of T is very lucky to have Professor Wood. Her examinations and assignments are incredibly fair, and if you put in the work you will be able to achieve a good mark. The course material is interesting too!

Dr Prichard is an excellent Professor.  He constantly pushes you to improve your work and think about all aspects of the subject matter.  You have to work it out for yourself sometimes, but this is what you need to do in order to succeed.

One of the worst professors at this institution. He actually turned me away from the subject. Lectures are dry and boring. Extremely unfair marker. Followed guidelines exactly for the midterm, and ended up getting a C- (I'm an A student). Very nit-picky marker, and comments made no sense. I caught him on his marking mistakes numerous times. Avoid.
Doesn't teach or prepare lectures, just rambles about occult theories

Christos is not only an extraordinary teacher, but also a quite thoughtful individual. Excellent.
Christos is the most AWESOME person I have ver met. He is BRILLIANT.

DO NOT TAKE A CLASS WITH THIS MAN!! He is so dry during lectures, shows up late half the time, and gives very vague and unhelpful feedback on tests and essays. Only do a class with him as a sure fire way to kill any remaining passions you had for the subject matter he covers.

comment: DO NOT TAKE A CLASS WITH LESK OH MY GOD!!!!!! His grading criteria is the worst I've ever seen, no rubric, no outline and incredibly vague. Course material is enjoyable and definitely unique, but quiz and test expectations are a bit vague, making the course more difficult than it should be. Attending and listening to lectures is crucial. Lesk isn't reachable by email. He posts incorrect deadlines, and doesn't provide accomodation. Professor Lesk is quite engaging in lectures, but his grading rubrics can be vague. Staying on top of the readings and attending class is key. For study help, I found unstuckstudy and ChatGPT to be useful supplements alongside the textbook.

Of my 4 years at uoft I have never met a ruder professor, his comments in essays are insane and completely uncalled for. Beware of his quizzes because there will be multiple right answers but if you don't pick what he would then too bad so sad. Also he is super unsupportive and does not respond to emails.

He gives multiple choice quizzes but many of the options could be considered correct but if you don't pick the one he chose then you're considered incorrect even if you give an explanation and show why your option was correct he won't care. He's not open to alternative views that differ from his own. This is difficult in an english class.

I found Lesk to have a pretentious nature about his class. His essay grading criteria are by far the weirdest I've seen from any of my classes, and I'm an English major. Was a fun professor! This was my favourite class this term. Would've preferred if it were in-person but he made the best of a bad deal

funny guy. really comprehensive and well thought out lectures. i hardly had to do any further explicating to write essays on the material - lesk gives you the information he wants you to write about. to be fair, he didn't provide rubrics and his essay criteria was often quite vague, so i think it was a bit lucky that my work was well received lol.

comment: Prof. Lesk gets a bad rapport on here and I'm not sure why. ENG235 was an amazing class and one of the only ones I was excited to show up to every week. comment:

Overall I enjoyed this course and I thought prof Lesk did a good job. He is very passionate about graphic novels and clearly knows what he's talking about. His lectures were dry, inconsistent, and most of the times, not helpful. Huge ego and no respect for students. Will not even try to care about what you have to say and will not care to learn who you are. Hated every second of class. Not open to students' opinions at all. Very vague with the way he explains mistakes. For an English professor he does not know how to speak in a polite way to students. Would not take a class again from him and would not recommend. You cannot be a professor just with a PhD ; people skills are needed too!

His lectures are pretty fun but I do notice that he sometimes goes off on a tangent, but do pay attention since the material does appear on the quizzes and assignments. comment: Such a funny and kind professor. Really enjoyed learning from him and contrary to what other reviews say he is accepting of other opinions and open to interpretations he just maintains his own views. Amazing class!!!

Andrew Lesk is a stellar professor. While he does have weekly essays they are only 500 words maximum. If you spend any time on these assignments you will get an A. You go on field trips around the city and discover a part of Toronto's history that all too many are unfamiliar with. I strongly recommend this as a breadth requirement course.

I don't know what's up with all the hate against Professor Lesk. I took his Short Story course last semester. Great and chill professor. Gave lots of time to complete the essay assignment. comment: Worst professor ever. Unrespectful, whenever you ask questions after class, he is so impatient. Very tough and negative grader. Sense of superiority.

Solid prof. His lectures contain everything you need to do well in the course, gives you plenty of time for tests and essays. Uses crude language often lol.

Prof. Lesk is underrated. I reckon the low scores come from the fact that he is not one of those happy-go-lucky professors; which, as far as I am concerned, is for the best. I personally think Andrew Lesk is a really under rater prof, he's really funny and despite what I've heard in my experience he is very accommodating as long as you go through him personally. Found this professor to be pretty mediocre. Lectures were a sleep fest consisting mostly of the prof ranting about irrelevant things. Watch out if you disagree with his opinions cause it will cost you.

Really disengaged prof. He's got high regard for his own ideas, but little time and patience for anyone who disagrees with him. Shows very little interest in student success, and does not make himself (or his TA's) accessible for any kind of assistance outside of lecture. Acts like he doesn't want to be there, and really couldn't care less.

Awful professor. He uses his lectures as a soapbox for his political views which have nothing to do with the course. His expectations on tests/assignments are very unclear, and he offers no help whatsoever. Prof. Lesk is the most uncaring, arrogant prof I have ever encountered. His classes are a waste of time and money.
Very very specific about what he wants out of your assignments. Needs you to pander to his own views to do well in the class, leaving not much room for originality and outside perspectives.

I was excited to take his Sex in the City one program, and the first term was okay, but the second he just piggy backed off of the other one program profs, and had very little to do with sexual diversity. He doesn't care for his students' opinions or mental health, and though some of the readings and trips were good, an overall disappointment.

The worst professor I've ever come across in my years at U of T. I would give him a 0/5 but it is not possible. Right from the get go, his ego is apparent. He does what suits him, and to heck about anyone else because of course the universe revolves around him. He's sad and I pity him. Save your money and time, and take a course with a better prof.

The 199 courses are great for breath requirements, and this course was no exception. It was a very fun course. There were only a few papers and one take home test. comment: Really arrogant, and just annoying. Really easy to get a good grade even though he's nit-picky.

comment: Really open to student's ideas, even when he didn't agree with them he accepted their merit. Really funny and used real world connections to make class interesting.

I LOVED Lesk's sex in the city class- would highly recommend this first year seminar. The material and field trips were very interesting and Lesk clearly knew a lot about the subject matter and added a lot to the overall experience. Sometimes it was hard to tell what kind of mood he was in which was scary, but for the most part he's a fun prof.

A few of us are currently having a study group for this class right now for the final exam. The problem we've noticed in the midterm is that even though our arguments are fully supported, which fulfills the requirement of a good essay/short answer, as long as he doesn't agree with your opinion, he will dispute the answer and give it a bad grade.
He is very opinionated and arrogant. His ego is through the roof.

I was very excited to take this course, as I'm new to the city and very interested in Sexual Diversity Studies. However, I find the course to often be a waste of time, unless we are on a field trip or there is a guest speaker. The assignments feel like busywork, and I find Prof. Lesk comes off as very arrogant, especially towards guests.

The worst! Anything that contradicts his argument he dismisses as "it doesn't matter cause it's just comics" THEN WHY ARE YOU TEACHING A COURSE ON THEM? In one class a girl called him out on taking a quote out of context, his response: "I know but it's so much more delicious this way." Great reading list but that's all.  AVOID HIM LIKE THE PLAGUE!!
The only way the professor grades you is essays, A LOT OF ESSAYS.   Write 3 essays in two hours in class...
Hes boring

Prof Lesk is an amazing speaker. His lectures are clear, concise, and very interesting. He grades fairly, but not too rough. I think the negative feedback for him on here must mostly be from people who didn't do their readings and consequently got poor marks. He doesn't put up with offensive opinions, but encourages discussion.

Completely arrogant, does not show any kind of care for his students, and gets upset when a student has an opinion that differs from his. I had high hopes for this course (graphic novels!) but he just made everything unpleasant. Try to avoid him at any cost.

He is unbearably condescending and unhelpful. At first I thought I was misreading him because sometimes people just sound dry over email, but nope! I took my concerns to him in person but he was just as rude. I did not enjoy being talked down to as if I were an idiot. Way to ruin an okay class.

Found him to be unnecessarily rude.  His comments on my essay had spelling errors.  It is amazing that U of T keeps him employed.  He provided no useful comments to me, and I am truly disappointed I selected his class.  If it was not a requirement for me, I would have dropped the course.  I advise all to stay away.  Wish I could get a refund.
I like that the course doesn't entirely focus on superheroes; I really enjoyed the pulp-type comics like Incognito. Also he's a total babe.
Most people didn't do well in this class. Topics are definitely interesting. He's a really hard marker. I really regret taking this class.

I took this course this summer even after reading most of these negative reviews and found none of them to be true. Prof. Lesk provoked class discussions where he was very receptive to every student's input - he had no ego, nor any sign of a temper. I thoroughly enjoyed the insights he gave for each graphic novel and found the exam to be fair.

I agree, he does ignore you if your ideas don't align if his. However, He chooses material and structures the course in such a way, that a good grade is not hard to achieve. This year he gave a "take-home" test, extended deadlines, used good texts and gave fair questions for the exam. Take him if you want a solid GPA or a flexible course.
He is not kind to his students. He only takes his own opinion into account and ignores everyone else. I dropped the course because I couldn't handle his ego.

It's not a bad class, but certainly not one of my favourites. Lesk's insights were fine, but I didn't think they were novel. I found his lecture style brusque, but I liked the syllabus. It's easy to do well if you use his ideas in the assignments. So overall, a good class for enthusiasts of graphic novels, but Lesk could've been better.

I also found his insights to be shallow. I found he made a number of points, but rarely went into any deep analysis of those points, which left much to be desired. It was quantity of over quality with this guy, and a lot of questions he brought up seemed to go unanswered. He also seemed somewhat unwelcoming of novel ideas brought up by students.

Extremely unhelpful and even rude at times. I did not feel like he cared at all about the students. His insights and analysis are extremely shallow, and he does not go into depth on any specific points. Everything he says, you can basically find online. I feel like I learned nothing from his class.
Super nice and laid back, easy class (guaranteed b at least).

I don't see what all the hype is about. His insights are that of a middle schooler and he wastes a ton of class time on "class discussion" which is neither helpful or constructive. Whenever he gets CLOSE to a salient point he seems to skirt around it. Also, his exams have nothing to do with what we spoke about in class (at length, anyway.)

He was a pretty interesting lecturer. Not boring. Provided extra help (tutorials) but they weren't mandatory which was nice. Favours those who talk in class, but sometimes he will just plain shut you down if he doesn't really agree with your point(s). Can feel degrading but how big of a deal that is depends on you.

if you have any ideas or opinions different from him, it is most likely that you'll get bad marks on everything. he's short-tempered and cranky. waste of my time. didn't like him at all. he teaches some courses that can be fun (ex. graphic novel) but he ruins it all!

I do not know what some of these reviewers are thinking! Lesk was a thought-provoking lecturer - why would any student not come to expect open-ended questions in a university English course?! I highly recommend Lesk: he encourages class participation, and his sense of humor permeates his articulate lectures. Look forward to learning from him again!

Lesk often raised interesting points in lectures. However, he raised numerous open-ended questions and often provided very little answers. Some information in lectures was repeated from essays I had seen online. He was difficult to approach; he often made me feel stupid and continued with the open-ended questions that didn't help very much.
i could have just as easily read academic essays online (from which he seemed to borrow liberally).    wildly unhelpful and condescending.

Honestly, didn't like him. He was very unwilling to allow for alternative explanations/ideas about symbols, and all-too-often completely dropped passages from the texts that could undermine his ideas. He was often cranky and short with students who simply had a different opinion than him. His book choices were pretty good and reasonable.

I've taken Lesk's classes for years, and I don't know what's happened with him. Maybe U of T has eaten his soul? He's not the same prof as he used to be. He's gotten grouchy and dry. I miss the early days; he used to be my favourite prof at this school.

Prof. Lesk is a great teacher.  He expects you to read the text, attend class and to participate (hence the reason why there are participation marks). If you like doing those things, you'll likely enjoy the class. If you don't, don't bother.

Although I did not take his short story or can fic class (where the majority of comments come from) I did take his Graphic Novel class in the summer. It was bloody brilliant. He is a nice guy, tough exterior, very clever- i got an A, and i dissented from his interpretations many times- although if you are conservative probably don't take it!

I had taken a class 2 years ago and it was fantastic... great lecturer and I learned a lot.  This year I intentionally hunted down a course he was teaching and it was awful.  He seemed miserable lecturing and the material tested on was not well covered and seemed random. Wish I had not taken the course.
The most banal insight imaginable on every text studied, and tests that rewarded only reiteration of dull, obvious lecture material. Brutal; avoid, avoid, avoid.

Lesk is a refreshing a lively prof. Material covered in class was delightful, i still reread the stories. He is an insightful and intelligent man and i would highly reccommend both his short story collection courses.

do not fall for his nice, humorous exterior! he marks impossibly. if you want to get by in class, use my advice: ...do not let him know you have a cell phone; do NOT come late; always talk in class. he is very bias, AND contrary to what he says, always regurgitate what he lectured about when it comes to the tests, it's the only thing he believes.

This Professor, while may have teaching skills, is one of the most biased and demeaning men I have ever met in my life. Not only does he cater towards those students that sit in the front that eagerly raise their hands every 5 five minutes )..but is very hard to deal with in regard to assignments. I wish I had not taken his class, he has ruined it.
Assessment techniques lack professionalism and are void of valid feedback. Comments are demeaning and hostile.

took short story with him, found him obscure and boring and looking only for you to write down what he wants. has favorites, lets brown nosers take 10 minutes to say something they could say in 15 seconds.
I had a hard time with this man.  He leaves a lot to be desired.  Not someone who teaches but rather lectures.  There is a big difference.  I would not have taken his class knowing what I know now.

Best Prof by far. Nice, smart, caring, despite what ppl are saying, he does listen to you & really encourages you to think critically. He is difficult but you are in university are you not? Listen to him, you are bound to benefit. ENG students especially, what he teaches you will help you in your approach in other ENG courses. BEST PROF EVER!

His midterm & exams require alot of writing (at least 3 essays)but he's one of the only profs who sticks to the text & dissects it for you. Extremely intelligent & enthusiastic. I usually skip most of my classes but never his, he's brilliant. If you really pay attention & read the text, you should do fine. Not a class for slacker thinkers though.

Brilliant Professor! Incredibly insightful and an english genius. My fave prof by far. Really nice, witty, but be careful of making stupid comments, he will question you. I didn't like some of his texts (nearly 500 pg book on prairie life, snore) but his other selections are bang on. Be prepared to pay attention but SO worth it.
straight forward communicator

Lectures were very interesting and he was very personable. The lectures were fun! Buuuut it was very difficult. The expectations for our first 50 minute test were way higher than the class expected, given the number of questions we had to answer in such a short amount of time. Be prepared to really be challenged! Tough marker!

Careerist garbage. Final essays were universally marked down according to arbitrary criteria not discernible from previous assignments, resulting in a low, bell-curved class average that could not be appealed.  Religiously PC, hostile to independence and originality.    Deliberately places intelligent students at a disadvantage. AVOID AT ALL COSTS!
since he is so young he's very up to date with his methods and contexts. he makes sure to compliment lectures with media that reflect our perspectives as students.

Although I was sometimes unsure where Lesk was going with his lectures, his class is one that comes together for me the more I think back on it. I think that he chose great novels and drew them together with valuable themes. I could do without some of his sexual anecdotes however. And... Lindy is one of the best TAs ever.
Great teacher.  Uses the word "ostensibly" like it is going out of style.

I agree with comments that he does tend to stick to a single interpretation of a literary work. This makes his lectures so dry you could start a fire with it. He also tends to pick on really minute details of a particular quote especially if it will reinforce his quote even if it has been beaten to death. But he seems nice as a person.
Very approachable and easy to communicate with. His lectures are clear and extrememly organized.

Lesk is a good speaker and brings precise critical analysis to the texts he chooses. He is approachable, effective and really knows his stuff. His use of theory (where applicable) was appreciated. There is no need to feel any trepidation towards taking his class; he is, for me, the best professor of my undergrad years.
No Comments

I participated in Lesk's Short Story Collection class, and was surprised by the formality of his opening lectures.  It seemed quite clear that any communication with him was to be strictly via ccnet, email, or excellent MLA formatting. This first impression was wrong...he's thorough, helpful (office hours) engaging, and an excellent professor.
I started enjoying class two months after it began. At the beginning he's very intimidating but also very easy on the eyes.
No Comments
Helpful, friendly, open to discussion

I'd advise people serious about English to stay away. He's not a very quick on the uptake & his analysis of texts is often strained. A tense, bitter guy who wears a suit every day (making up for his academic inadequacy?) There's something I like about him, but his "interpretations" & lack of listening skills drive me (& most of the class) insane.

Despite his own ideas of grandeur professor Lesk is just a minor undergraduate prof. at the U of T. He doesn’t even teach 400 level English courses, has no position as a permanent member of the Faculty of English and doesn’t even have tenure. The comments that many students have sent are true in regards to how he treats the opinions of others. Don’

Most of the comments, as mentioned are quite true.  I did notice that when he would make a point, he would ask the class for the answer, and in return, it would never be answered.  He would go off topic or just change the subject, so I was left with an unanswered question in my notebook.  He does have his own views and tends to stick with them.

Hilarious and brilliant Prof.  His lectures are clear, and he makes the content really interesting.  He always breaks for 15 minutes to take questions from students, and provide further insight.  His sense of humour is often mistaken for arrogance, but he's really just having fun with lecture and his students.
Loved his lectures. They are straightforward and helpful. It would be more helpful if he could upload the lecture slides.

One of 2 lecturers in the course. Early on asked the class of 1500 "who here is a communist?" One poor sap put his hand up and Kopstein replied "Your responsible for x million deaths" Besides that strange interaction,a prof whose lectures I looked forward to. Clips form Failsafe and Dr. Strangelove, a unique analysis of the pogroms, and civil war.

Kopstein may come off as arrogant, but he's a really fun professor. Totally enthusiastic and has a great sense of humour. While I'm not much of a politics person and sucked at the class, I was still so engaged during his lectures. DO YOUR READINGS!

Did a great job of explaining the materials. He is a brilliant speaker but can very easily be mistaken for being arrogant. Doing the readings (all online, no textbook) will do you great service as the exam is mostly based on it. Marking can be harsh b/c of the number of students in the class. Attend tutorials and take advantage of your TA!

Great prof; funny and passionate lectures; makes politics interesting. His attempt at a Canadian accent = definitely a highlight of first year. Signed up for the class thinking I'd drop it and ended up majoring in Political Science instead.
his lectures do not have much to do with the essays and midterm. he talks alot, and seems arrogant.
Took this class a couple of years ago before POL101 was created. He is the reason I am a Poli sci major; easily one of the best profs at UofT. Pulling an A- wasn't that difficult.
He's interesting and good looking but I got no real knowledge out of him. He keeps on talking but you don't really take notes or anything. Nevertheless, he's quite interesting and funny.
Excellent lecturer. Engaging, charismatic, intelligent. Initially, he came across as rather arrogant and intimidating, but overall, challenging and compelling prof.

I had him a few years ago for POL103 - now he teaches POL101 with another Prof. Kopstein is very smart, knowledgeable, and one of the best Profs at U of T. He is not easy. Jumping into Marx and Weber in 100 level course is tough. However they new course POL101 maybe easier?
Charismatic. If you don't care for politics, he'll still keep you enthralled. It was a thrill and a pleasure to listen to him lecture for 2 hours.

A decent presenter but his thinking is too black/white, and the lectures were too dumbed down. He likes to be dramatic and spends alot of time explaining the moral failings of the Soviet Union rather than describing their organization, and telling us how we do not understand what it is like to "live in fear" (like in the cold war).

He seemed arrogant at first, but hey, that's Kopstein, he's the same with other profs. Enlivened the Weber & Marx material.  His tests are essentially lecture based, so pay attn!  With a little effort & attn, an 80% is in your future. Caution: TAs may mark hard on 1st essay, but are easy on the 2nd.

He is very engaging and charismatic.  His enthusiasm made me feel like I was in a church and he was the preacher.  Overall a good teacher.  Though, sometimes, at the end of the lecture I was not quite sure I grasped the concepts as our T.A. would summarize it a whole different way
Kopstein was an excellent lecture. He took readings that would otherwise be dry (i.e. Weber), and made them relevant and interesting. Also, his humour, wit, and dry sarcasm made the class memorable.
Fantastic lecturer. Thought I couldn't love polisci more then I came to his class and was proved wrong!
awesomeeee interesting teacher!
Brilliant lecturer. Funny, intelligent, charismatic. Very easy to remain focused and concentrated in class. Also helps that the subject matter is great.

Kopstein teaches the only intro course at UofT now because no other prof can do it the way he can. He brings the reading material, which is heavy, straight to the student. It makes sense when he presents it, so don't miss lectures. Talk to him before writing essays.  His TAs are all exceptional btw.

LOVED HIM. He may seem arrogant at first but you will love him for it. Very intellegent man and does allow student to voice opinions and ask questions. He corrects and makes jokes when approriate. The TA's are not the greatest but you will love going to lecture so don't worry! Highly recommended! Perfect for first year students :)
HILARIOUS guy, extremely down-to-earth, casual but not sloppy, definitely unforgettable.
Smart and witty.

The ONLY reason I wake up at 8 AM... ever... is for Kopstein's class. However, since it's supposed to be a world politics course, I would appreciate not ignoring the entire continent of South America...
Memorable jokes, pretty cool guy

A touch egomaniacal, but he can be quite engaging to listen to. Heavy workload to start with, then quickly lightens up. Does have a good sense of humour. Always chats with students on the lecture break, only clashes with the egomaniacal students. And he IS an expert on East European politics. Interesting guy, whether you like him or not.

If it wasn't for him I wouldn't be in European Studies. Also, his enthusiasm for the course material was very encouraging for me to do the readings and actually pay attention. Great prof and I like the way he lectures.

I second the egomaniac assessment.  Knowledgeable but a bit self-obsessed. Not terribly interested or concerned in students, seemed bored having to teach us most of the time. Still, pretty easy grader - not a high hurdle to overcome.

He is excellent at explaining his material. Whatever he explains, you understand. He commands respect and  demands competence from his students.I see that he shows off unintentionally and spontanously (which adds to his humour and charisma), and even then he's honest about what he doesn't know! He has to go down a bit on the showing off.

An amazing Professor, smart, funny, entertaining, and engaging. He brings the material to life. He comes across like a hard ass at times but he isn't, show him respect and he will show you respect back. Certainly his expectations are high and the work load is heavy. He is a fundamentally decent man. I have the highest regard for him.

An amazing prof.  Smart, funny, great speaker, clear.  As a first year student, I am honoured to have him as my instructor for a course i'm very interested in.  I really like the way he presents the material, in a very naturally flowing speech that shows he understands it very well and i learn well in that manner.
My favourite professor by far! I think he is the only one who could fill an auditorium at 9 in the morning. I really enjoyed going to lecture. He is smart, funny, and pretty damn attractive.
The best Prof I've had yet. If you go to lecture, you'll be fine. Extremely clear, and also very entertaining. I actually wanted to be in this class at 9 in the morning.
Lectures very funny and informative. Actually looked forward to class, tho it was at 9am. TA was surprisingly good. Be sure to look at previous years exams.
Incredible prof! Presented class with interesting and valuable material. Definitely a comedian....I laughed more than I took notes...but the lectures stuck!

this prof is by far the best ive had in the past 4 years..hes intelligent, charismatic, funny and inspiring..he made what we were learning come to life..i would take his class over and over again if i could..if you have the chance to take his class do it - you wont regret it..
oh my god , soooooo hot, hot hot hot , i would date him if it was legal or i would sleep with him for extra marks.
Good prof, interesting lectures, allocates lots of time for questions, course title is misleading (has little to do with Canada), final exam was almost identical to last year's and was easy

Exceptionally biased, which isn't that big a problem most of the time, but he does not state his biases.  Instead he goes off making fun of animal rights, non-mainstream ideologies, etc. effectively discouraging discourse and presents opinions as facts.  Be very wary and critical when taking his classes.  Also did not teach anything about Canada.

By far my best lecturer in 1st year! His lectures were organized, interesting and fairly clear.  And if he wasn't lecturing the guy could be a stand-up comedian!  His dry humour is priceless! Only criticism is that we barely did anything on Canadian politics.  Still, Kopstein will definitely go down as one of the epic profs at U of T.

My favourite prof during my 4 years of undergrad.  His lectures were very clear and organised and his jokes made them enjoyable... it was like 2 hours of stand-up comedy.  The one class in University that I never skipped.
Excellent lecturer, plenty of enthusiasm.  If you can't understand the concepts the way he teaches them you shouldn't be in university.
An excellent, intelligent, and commanding professor worthy of your mind.
Awesome.  He is one of the best profs I ever had.
Great teacher! His lectures are amazing!
Lectures are very interesting. There is too much emphasis on communism, Marxism and Weber and not enough on comparative politics from a Canadian perspective.

he's a pretty good teacher, but he goes a little too fast sometimes. when you come to class, don't fall alseep, you'll miss all the points and do not copy his slides word for word, you just get lost afterwards because he expands on the points when he speaks and that is the most important part.

Kopstein: unfriendly arrogant unhelpful--but it doesn't matter so much. Your mark depends on TAs. Try to get the Eastern European TA or the Asian TA--NOT Josh (late most of tutorials; random kindergarten discusses of what you liked/disliked; he may be cute but won't get you marks) Final exam concerns textbook readings; Midterm on reader.

An interesting course taught by a prof who knows what he's doing. The lectures -- for the most part -- were interesting even though the readings were horribly long. The TA was great help but Kopstein made the course material bearable. A recommended class for POL students. P.S. You can sometimes catch Kopstein on TVO.

2 hr 9am lectures could have easily been summarized in 20 min. Too much distastefully self-conscious lecturing "techniques" (IE. his supposedly manufactured arrogance) not enough original analysis. The $90 text, edited by him, is a collection of enycyclopediac information with far too much historical detail. Sensational instead of thoughtful.
Kopstein was awesome.

A professor you will remember your entire university career, whether you like him or not.  His arrogance would not be smiled upon if possesed by any other prof., but his sense of humour masks and justifies it all at once.  Assignments are tough, though it's not impossible to get an A.

Kopstein's great! Always got through his stuff, always hits the major points, always answers all questions! only drawback about this course are the readings - a lot of them too boring and he hardly ever refers to them in class anyway. Overall though it's a great course and you'll have a great time!
No Comments
Doesn't have a clue sometimes abotu certain topics, but still decides to comment.

He's really funny, although a bit on the nasty-humour side sometimes.  Good lecturing style, keeps you awake.  Pretty good dealing with questions in class, listens to students.  Assignments were a ***** though.  Said he wanted lots of chili peppers!

Amazing professor!! His enthusiasm is infectious and his sense of humour made the class even more interesting. Kopstein is also able to make the material relevant by relating it back to current events or his own personal stories, which bring the lecture to life. Awesome Prof!!

Took this class for Poli Sci. distribution...wish I had gotten into POL108. Some say he has charisma, I just find Kopstein incredibly annoying. Studying Marx, Engels, Weber = horrible. this prof is by far the best ive had in the past 4 years..hes intelligent, charismatic, funny and inspiring..he made what we were learning come to life..i would take his class over and over again if i could..if you have the chance to take his class do it - you wont regret it..
GREAT PROF! VERY UNDERSTANDING AND INFORMATEIVE!

This prof reminds me of a younger version of Letterman. He's definitely one of those profs you'll remember for being so funny,charismatic,honest, and cool as heck.But he always goes off on these tangents and is wayy too broad/general in his lectures. He asked for peppers, so he's getting one. Kopstein is great. I have found him to be enthusiastic, engaging, intelligent and  relitively accessible(especially for a departmental director).
Asked for pepper.  Ask and ye shall receive.  Had him for POL 181 also, found him a good prof.  Lecture style fairly engaging.  Material maybe not so much. (European Integration? :/ )
Prof JK likes hot peppers! :P Great prof; very funny, very enthusiastic about material, very interesting, very approachable; GREAT JOB!

You can only have a professor like him once in a lifetime, both understandable and understanding. The class is very interesting and the conversations are led by him in an excellent and enjoyable way. He is the kind of professor that a student always remembers with respect and admiration.
Great course. Excellent TA marker - received very helpful comments!  I would recommend this course to anyone!

here's the truth on kopstein, he's a professor that can make dry material interesting (even if you hate the stuff), he marks fairly, he uses powerpoint for notes every week, and the books don't cost much. Take his course b/c you'll prob. get a good mark.
EXTREMLY arrogant. biased. both unattractive qualities in a first year political science prof. If you didnt agree with him and his TA's you were basically screwed.
Great lectures, good discussion. Not always available during the office hours. Overall enjoyable course. Go for it.

Extremely fluent in course material taught.  Has some of the WORST TA's...so watch out for that.  But overall, he's great speaker and his lectures are definitely worth going to.  I enjoyed his class thouroughly!
On several occasions, I found him to be pompous, arrogant, and extremely pro-American. I couldn't wait for this course to end.

Very unenjoyable. On more than one occasion he has stopped 500 person lectures to yell at people coming or leaving and pick on people who whisper. He claims he doesn't let his political views get in the way, and then he lets the class leave to protest.
Nice guy, but he has the worst TA's on campus!  Also, he's too hard for first year!
Overall, he's a nice guy and knows his stuff, but he picks some of the WORST t.a's!....I had to appeal everything, and got higher marks!
Material is not the most appealing subject, but he's pretty clear about it.  And people, you weren't supposed to copy the slides, you were supposed to take notes off the lecture.
HE ROCKS!
knows he's the ****, and is a wry **** but that meks him so much hotter. assignments were way too difficult for first year.
Kopstein is witty and makes the material very interesting -- he's a good lecturer, although the downside is that he knows he's a good lecturer
Quirky and funny, but it won't make his boring material more appealing. Also speeds through his very long slides like it's the end of the world
A good prof who doesn't tolerate **** in class. Good in a 500 person lecture, but not sure I would want a seminar with him.
He's unapprochable, boring, and very impatient, class is also really bad.
Crazy, strange, very intelligent, witty/humorous, knows his ****, quotes austin powers and the godfather and he's very philosophical, approachable....great guy and great prof
Socratic method at its worst

I am a straight-A student for all other courses and he is the only prof that gave me a very poor mark even though I work hard for it. The course slide is not clear is messed up. Not recommended to take this course with this professor.
Don't sleep through his class.  Very good professor.

Overall the class was alright.  One note though, don't make yourself noticed, or sit in the first 5 rows.  He will make fun of you quite often (which was the case this past year).  I will hopefully use what I learned sometime in the future, but I do not wish to ever take another course with him, or really help him out in a significant manner.
Great Professor. Good class. Helpful when you need him. One -ve - It was sometimes difficult to follow his notes. Overall - would love to take another course with him.
great awesome prof who's hilarious and engaging to his students

Material is easy enough, but the prof is insufferable.  Patronizing and condescending, he never employs humility, or even considers the possibility that the students -- bankrolling his academic gravy train by way of their grandiose tuition -- might be of intelligence equal to or greater than his own. Pressnail you are THE MAN.  Love your lectures, love your teaching style. Would take any course that you teach even classical algebra. Keep up the good work.
One of the best profs I ever had. He is fun and he uses fun ways to teach. His lectures are pure enjoyment.
Speeds through material, sometimes a little too fast.  Incredibly entertaining, however, and his classes are definitely worth the tuition fees.
One of the best profs I have ever had. Sees beyong the traditional scope of engineering. Passionate. Hilarious. Engaging.
Brilliant Engineer and Lawyer,stimulating and complete in his presentation,a review at the beginning of concurrent lectures would be a positive.
HE is the best prof ever don't diss him he has won prof of the year for like ever!!! Be nice and just because he talks about his hair doesn't mean that he is arogant!!
very easy and helpful, also entertaining

Very helpful during office hour! He stayed past the scheduled office hour time to make sure he got to every student and answered all their questions. He did not just give out the answers but encouraged critical thinking and helped catch mistakes to get unstuck on tough questions.

I've had him twice, before and during covid. Before covid, he was very helpful and provided all necessary readings for the class to succeed, including practice questions and solutions to them. In covid, the course was very unprepared, unorganized and poorly taught. This was early in covid so I want to be fair since he was a great prof before covid.

One of the most poorly organized courses I've ever taken. Kept delaying the problem sets to the point where he had to cancel one of them, and gave us all 100 on it. Said he would have grades for part 2 of project back a few days before deadline for part 3, but didn't. Our final 'exam' was barely an exam.

Not a good instructor. Had this class over the summer online and it was really terribly managed. Actual lecturing was not engaging and the teaching style was extremely boring. Luckily lectures were recorded so that helped a lot. Actual grading was fair, but course structure and organization was a nightmare.
this summer 263 was organized horribly, maybe its the school's fault maybe it is his fault but i genuinely had a really bad experience

Course was so unorganized. Instructor kept screwing up problem sets. He had trouble doing some simple proofs by induction, copying from his notes and stopping when his notes were too messy and not being able to finish the proofs by hand. Would never take his class again. If possible take this course with David or Danny (the better Heap).

comment: Took this class online during COVID-19 but Prof. Roorda was very accommodating, thorough in his lectures and did numerous examples for us. Assignments were straight forward. Midterm was a little lengthy but not difficult. Term project had slightly unclear expectations but you can still do a great job. Wouldn't mind if he taught all the CIV courses.
10/10 Great guy, Pretty good father too... Word up...
Very good and FAIR professor...expects u to UNDERSTAND what hes teaching once you do so ur good to go

Lectures are pretty monotone and dry-simply slides with formulas/definitions/graphs straight from text. I guess it's not the prof but the course-he is a overall a nice and fair guy. Despite best intentions, could not help falling asleep during the Friday 2hr lecture. Class was grateful (except 2 people) he offered an alternate outline/exam weight.
Great class, learned a lot. Prof. Sorkhou is very knowledgeable and helpful.

this guy teaches irrelevant material in lecture and doesnt provide practice problems for exams causing exams to be very difficult to be 40-50 avg range with no bell curve at all. He uses passive aggressive tone when he catches students cheating... do not take the course with him
Prof. Sorkhou is very caring about his students and teaches concepts clearly and well!
Great guy! Teaches very clearly with many examples. We had an open source textbook but it wasn't even necessary because he was so good.

such an organised and competent prof, replies quickly, grades quickly, does exactly as she promises and in general is just super warm. Material (Digital Gov't) is interesting, but course is disorganized/repetitive. Craft is knowledgeable but robotic; doesn't get student perspectives. comment: Professor Craft is a fine lecturer, and he evidently knows a lot about the subject matter, but his classes can often hew too closely to the textbook, and as a result, aren't nearly as engaging or interesting as they could be. Still, a nice guy who knows a lot about Canadian politics.
The prof is trying his best. However, as a lecturer he is lackluster and cannot hold the attention of his student. Please start taking a break at the halfway point of a 2 hour lecture.
