comment: Prof Sean was kind, understanding and passionate about forest conservation. He gave the entire class multiple extensions (during the pandemic) and invited guest speakers to keep the course engaging. The assignments were not difficult but very, very time consuming and sometimes seemed irrelevant to lectures/not really showing what you've learned.

This course is pretty different due to the online format; some assignments are kinda weird. If you've taken BIO120 most content is review; new content isn't too hard. Most of the assignments can be finished in 1-2 days if you're a bio/forestry student. Main gripe is vague mark schemes. Professor is clearly passionate and lectures aren't too long.

Horrible. Its like he makes it a point to prove that this isnt a bird course, which he tries so hard by making the assignments so difficult and time consuming when its not necessary at all. Hated this course and took way too much time. This prof is weird too
Did not enjoy this course at all. Midterm and exam included a lot of blurry pictures and were quite irrelevant from the given guides.
Passionate about what he teaches. He wants you to enjoy the learning process, and not so much studying.
Great professor and a nice guy.

Sean is very knowledgable and always willing to help. He's passionate about his field of work and that is what makes him really great at teaching what he does. His class will change your mind about the UofT experience.

The professor was helpful, professional and was not only professional but respectful of all students. He also used different teaching approaches such as having guest lecturers throughout the semester, interactive assignments, group assignments and he even had a musical review for the final exam in! How cool is that?  FOR201 literally rocked.

Sean is an expert in his field and does a wonderful job communicating and simplifying such a vast amount of knowledge and information to his students. Attending lectures is an advantage because he explains slides that have a few words on them and sometimes he even stresses the most important or big picture slidesinformation. Put in the effort.

The professor was enthusiastic and clear while lecturing. He also helped in preparing us for tests. The assignments for the course are not overwhelming but it does take some effort in order to get an A. If you're not into environmental studiesforestry then the course may be a drab.

FOR201 taught by Prof. Sean Thomas, was a delightful experience that was engaging challenging and inspirational. An enthusiastic lecturer who will bend over backwards to ensure a students sucess, if they choose. Albeit a difficult course, I would truly recommend as this is a unique course and the professor brings a positive and valuable dynamic.
Super dorky, but really cool. This class made an English Major interested in Tropical Forestry!
Great lecturer, passionate about the subject and even put on a little concert for us with forestry themes. Its not an easy course but not impossible just dont expect to get good grades with no effort
Lectures were really clear and he is clearly very passionate about the subjects. A lot of people came in expecting a super easy joke course and are just grumpy they didn't get an easy A
He is super genius and ignites sprite in you!
Sean is pure genius coupled with immense curiosity. His assignments represent real applications. He is fair, honest, and approachable. Possibilities for quality research extend beyond the course.
The guidelines for this course were very ambiguous.  It was difficult to determine what was expected of students, as it was not clearly communicated.

Umm, forestry should really be in the list of university depts.  Sean is a genius who has retained a child-like curiousity for most forest-related topics.  A tough yet fair marker.  a great writer and communicator.  if you're into forest ecology (or stats), tree physiology, or mites, he's your man.

Im not exaggerating when I say shes the nicest, most compassionate prof out there. She was so considerate of how difficult online learning is and made everything accessible (literally typed out a transcript for part of her lecture bc she THOUGHT she spoke too fast). This woman never stops smiling and motivating students - an absolute angel.
Amazing prof and just the kindest person. She was so understanding throughout the semester, and always answered emails quickly. I will miss her!

Under Professor Andreapoulos, BCH311 used to be a very difficult and boring course. Professor Fussner completely transformed this course into an easy and fun one! It truly is amazing how much better a course could be when a different course coordinator is running the same material!

If you are ever lucky enough to be her student, you should donate whatever amount you can afford to your charity of choice! She is the epitome of balancing professionalism and friendliness. She provides the absolute best for her students to succeed in her course and will always go out of her way to help you as your professor and your mentor.

This prof is amazing all around. She is considerate of her students. The amount of work in her class should honestly be set as the standard for other u of t classes. The assignments were flexible enough to let me learn more about what I want to learn. Heck even her lecturing voice itself is calming. Again, simply amazing.

I would NOT take her again, simply because she is the kindest prof that exists in UofT and I might just take advantage of that in the future... She's such a gem and a sweet person. Professors like her are why I still have hope in BCH department.

Very caring prof! Workload was not heavy but very meaningful. She is easily accessible outside of class, very accommodating, approachable, welcoming, supportive. comment: Had him 3 times. He's very passionate about logic. Clear and fair course structure. I think everybody appreciated not having a final exam. He was very helpful at office hours and nice to all students even if you never come to class.

He's a great prof who is very understanding! Truly passionate about the subject and has a lot of insight. The class had a lot of dense assigned readings per week tho. Quite a bit of writing too, but he's a fair marker. You'll do well if you put in the effort.

excellent prof who cares a lot about his students while clarifying any material that has been misunderstood

comment: clear and well composed in class

comment: Attended his undergraduate and joint undergraduate/graduate courses in 1985!!!  One of the best professors I have had. Clear and engaging, his lectures were a joy. But perhaps the best thing about Michael Wayne is that he listens to his students and takes their input seriously.

THE GREATEST. She's like the Muhammed Ali of professors. Incredible lectures, so smart. She's wonderfully friendly and always ends lectures with a mic drop. I cannot recommend her enough. Seriously, she's amazing. My favorite prof I've ever had. SO SO GOOD!!!

This class was my favorite of the year and the only one I would consistently attend and enjoy! Seriously, if you're only going to take one english course you're whole uni career make sure it's this one and if you're into modern literature, you will love this course!
